text:
marta: Hey — trying the docker-compose quickstart and my first call is a 403 with "billing_required". Console shows "workspace not provisioned". Anyone seen this when using SSO org + service account?

alex: Do you see the same workspace in the console billing page (Settings -> Billing)? sometimes new workspaces don't get auto-provisioned.

marta: Pasted minimal output from the sample app container:
```
POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
Content-Type: application/json

HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{
  "error": "billing_required",
  "message": "workspace w-k7f... not linked to billing"
}
```

devstack-bot: :rotating_light: New workspace created for marta@acme.co. Billing status: unverified. See <https://console.redwood.example/workspaces/w-k7f...|workspace page>.

jamie: Two quick checks: 1) Is that token a user SSO session (short-lived) or a service key? Docker-compose quickstart expects a service key env var, not an interactive SSO token. 2) If you just added a card, provisioning can be ~5–10m delayed.

marta: Ugh we do SAML SSO + org policy requires MFA and blocks service keys by default. I don't see a "create service key" option in the console (only personal tokens).

alex: If org policy disables service keys, you can: a) ask your org admin to enable service/token creation for that project, or b) create a dedicated project under a billing-verified org and invite the service account. For quickstart local testing the simplest is a short-lived personal token but that breaks CI.

jamie: I can add a clearer error in the quickstart that detects "billing_required" and prints a helpful hint + link. Also adding a note about SSO orgs and service-key requirement. Will open an issue.

sre-oncall: FYI, we've seen a race where workspace creation + billing attach finishes but the billing flag isn't returned for ~2 min due to cache. If you hit 403 immediately after card add, wait 120s and retry.

olivia: Support here — if you DM me the workspace id I'll check whether service keys are blocked by org policy and can temporarily enable one for your test.

marta: Workspace id is w-k7f9b2. Thanks, DMing now. Also: proposal — quickstart docker-compose should validate env var name (REDWOOD_API_KEY) and error clearly when the token scope is wrong. I wasted ~30m swapping tokens.

jamie: Agreed. I'll: 1) add token-scope validation + clearer message, 2) add a short wiki on SSO org steps (admin flow to allow service tokens), 3) file a small change to the sample compose file to call out the env var name. Opening issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/devex/isssues/542 (will fix this week).

alex: Once support confirms org policy, we can add an extra CI test that runs quickstart against a restricted org to catch this earlier.

marta: Thanks all — workaround worked (used a service key via support). First successful call now. Leaving notes in our onboarding doc for the team. :party_parrot:
